# Summary: Conservative Party Manifesto 2024

## Economic Policy and Taxation

The manifesto proposes halving employee National Insurance from 12% to 6% by April 2027, representing a £1,350 tax reduction for average workers earning £35,000. The party commits to abolishing the main rate of self-employed National Insurance by Parliament's end, affecting four million people.

For pensioners, the "Triple Lock Plus" would ensure State Pension and personal allowance rise with inflation, earnings, or 2.5%, preventing the State Pension from becoming subject to income tax. Child Benefit thresholds would shift to household-based assessment, with benefits retained until combined income reaches £120,000.

The party pledges to maintain fiscal rules requiring public sector debt to fall and borrowing to remain below 3% of GDP.

## Immigration and Border Security

A legally binding migration cap would be introduced, with Parliament voting annually on levels. Skilled Worker visa salary thresholds have increased to £38,700. The Rwanda removal scheme would continue, with asylum claims processed within six months. International asylum treaty reform is proposed.

## Defence and National Security

Defence spending would increase to 2.5% of GDP by 2030, with £10 billion invested in munitions production. A mandatory National Service programme for 18-year-olds would offer military placements or community volunteering.

## Housing and Infrastructure

The party targets 1.6 million new homes, focusing on brownfield development in major cities. First-time buyer Stamp Duty exemptions would be made permanent up to £425,000, with a new Help to Buy scheme. Leasehold reform continues, including ground rent caps.

£36 billion from cancelled HS2 Phase 2 would fund regional transport improvements, including £8.3 billion for road maintenance.

## Healthcare and Public Services

NHS spending would increase above inflation annually, with plans for 92,000 additional nurses and 28,000 more doctors. Mental health support would expand, including coverage in all schools by 2030. Social care cost caps would proceed from October 2025.

## Energy and Environment

The party commits to net zero by 2050 while pledging no new green levies. Annual North Sea oil and gas licensing would continue. Nuclear power expansion includes Small Modular Reactors approval. Offshore wind capacity would triple.

## Education and Skills

The Advanced British Standard would reform 16-19 education. Funding would support 100,000 additional apprenticeships, partially funded by closing underperforming university courses. Mobile phones would be banned during school hours.
